A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OAIMS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original fundus and brain-MRI segmentation experiments, numerical comparisons, ablations, and robustness analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds held-out adaptation data-efficiency results in Appendix A.11 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The U-Net inputs, CCG and Dice–Focal losses, two-stage Post-Interaction adaptation, and Mid-Interaction updates remain unchanged. Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2 describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five fundus and four brain-MRI databases and segmentation tasks. The new data-efficiency study uses retained ATLAS, BraTS T1, and WMH FLAIR coverage; its held-out splits change evaluation design.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds a comparison of OAIMS adaptation learning curves against an automatic model trained on the target distribution. This comparator type already appeared in Figure 2, but its participation in this adaptation-efficiency comparison is new. Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.11 adds separate adaptation/evaluation splits: 554/100 ATLAS images, 199/50 BraTS T1 images, and 40/20 WMH FLAIR images. Adaptation uses ten clicks per image; held-out Dice is measured every five adaptation images using ten simulated clicks without updating on evaluation images. Existing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix A.11 and Figure 7 investigate how many target images are needed for adaptation to improve held-out performance across three MRI targets. Existing component ablations, click-budget studies, noisy-click tests, and source-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 retains its three-seed averaging, and the Gaussian-width analysis retains its individual run examples. Figure 7 adds no reported run counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–18 and existing plotted results are unchanged. Figure 7 adds learning curves: for example, ATLAS held-out Dice rises from below 0.55 before adaptation to above 0.80 after approximately 30 images. These are new results under a separate protocol, not revisions of earlier benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the Gaussian and class-indicator definitions, pseudo-ground-truth assumptions, and mathematical descriptions of the losses are retained. No theoretical result, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: CCG-enhanced interactive segmentation and complementary Post-Interaction and Mid-Interaction adaptation under distribution shift. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.11 interprets the new curves as evidence that adaptation needs relatively few target images and can reduce subsequent correction effort. This adds a sample-efficiency interpretation; existing mechanism explanations, robustness interpretations, and applicability qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code and pretrained models with a specific code-repository link, making access instructions concrete. The PDFs alone do not establish repository contents or pretrained-model availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to interactive segmentation, online adaptation, and unsupervised losses are unchanged. Minor wording edits do not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and acknowledgment edits, adds the data-efficiency subsection, and moves the LLM-use disclosure from A.6 to A.12 with corresponding appendix renumbering. The main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 7, reduces Figure 6's display size, relocates Tables 12 and 16, and adds conference headers. Table 8's caption is lightly reworded; existing figure content and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.11 and Figure 7 add useful evidence about how quickly adaptation benefits held-out images, a practical question not quantified in v2. The code link also improves access documentation. The gain is limited: the scientific core is unchanged, and the new curves lack reported run variability and competing adaptation-method learning curves, limiting broader comparative efficiency conclusions.
